2607.16065.title: Spatial Normalization for Cross-Domain Retinal Layer Segmentation in Optical Coherence Tomography
2607.16065.paper_summary: Retinal layer segmentation in Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is a fundamental step for extracting quantitative biomarkers of retinal structure. Indeed, there is a growing interest in the analysis of OCTs in the context of neurodegenerative diseases. However, segmentation remains challenging due to speckle noise, shadowing artifacts, low contrast between adjacent layers, anatomical variability across subjects, and domain shifts arising from different acquisition protocols and clinical populations. While deep learning methods have achieved remarkable performance, their robustness and generalization across heterogeneous datasets remain limited. In this work, we investigate the role of spatial normalization as a preprocessing strategy to mitigate geometric domain shifts and improve the consistency of retinal layer segmentation. Inspired by standard practices in neuroimaging, we introduce a fovea-centered normalization framework that aligns OCT volumes into a common anatomical reference. We perform a comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures. To provide a comprehensive assessment of segmentation quality, we combine conventional overlap-based metrics at B-scan level with topology-aware metrics at A-scan level and thickness-based measures at the en-face level. In cases where a ground truth is not available, we propose topology violation quantitative metrics that do not require ground truth annotations and a thickness-based qualitative assessment that captures structural consistency and clinically relevant patterns at the en-face level. The results demonstrate the importance of spatial normalization in OCT segmentation pipelines toward the development of robust and clinically meaningful retinal analysis tools, enabling reliable biomarker extraction and downstream computational analysis in neurodegenerative research.
2607.16065.paper_summary_zh: 視網膜層分割在光學相干斷層掃描（OCT）中是提取視網膜結構定量生物標記的基本步驟。<lb/>的確，對於在神經退行性疾病背景下分析OCT的興趣日益增長。<lb/>然而，由於斑點噪聲、陰影伪影、相鄰層之間的低對比度、受試者之間的解剖變異性，以及由不同獲取協議和臨床人群引起的領域轉移，分割仍然具有挑戰性。<lb/>儘管深度學習方法已取得顯著的表現，但其在異質數據集上的穩健性和泛化能力仍然有限。<lb/>在本研究中，我們探討了空間正規化作為預處理策略的作用，以減輕幾何領域轉移並改善視網膜層分割的一致性。<lb/>受到神經影像學標準實踐的啟發，我們引入了一個以中央凹為中心的正規化框架，將OCT體積對齊到共同的解剖參考。<lb/>我們對最先進的深度學習架構進行了全面評估。<lb/>為了提供對分割質量的全面評估，我們將基於B掃描的傳統重疊度量與基於A掃描的拓撲感知度量和基於面掃描的厚度度量相結合。<lb/>在沒有真實標準的情況下，我們提出了不需要真實標準標註的拓撲違規定量度量，以及一種基於厚度的定性評估，捕捉結構一致性和臨床相關模式。<lb/>結果顯示，空間正規化在OCT分割管道中的重要性，促進了穩健且臨床有意義的視網膜分析工具的發展，使得在神經退行性研究中能夠可靠地提取生物標記和進行下游計算分析。
